paragraphs.title: A Call to All Nations to Praise the Lord

easy.explanation: The verse begins, “O praise the LORD, all ye nations.”
easy.q: Who is called to praise the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “praise him, all ye people.”
easy.q: What are all the people told to do?

easy.explanation: “Nations” refers to different peoples or countries.
easy.q: What does the word “nations” mean in this verse?

answers: Both phrases give a wide call to praise the LORD
The phrases refer only to one family
The second phrase cancels the first
medium.explanation: The two phrases emphasize that the call to praise includes every nation and people.
medium.q: What relationship does the verse show between “all ye nations” and “all ye people”?

answers: To honor and speak well of someone
medium.explanation: To praise the LORD is to honor and speak well of Him.
medium.q: What does the word “praise” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: The central command of the verse is to praise the LORD.
medium.q: What is the main command in Psalm 117:1?

answers: The verse concerns only the past
challenge.explanation: Repeating “all” shows that no nation or people is excluded from the call to praise.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repetition of “all” in the verse?

answers: They reinforce the call to praise the LORD
They express doubt about praising God
challenge.explanation: Both commands urge the nations and peoples to praise the LORD.
challenge.q: How do the commands “O praise” and “praise him” function in the verse?

answers: Every nation and people is summoned to honor the LORD
Only Israel is commanded to worship
The nations are warned to avoid the LORD
challenge.explanation: The verse gives every nation and people a direct summons to praise the LORD.

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Enduring Kindness and Truth

easy.explanation: The verse says, “For his merciful kindness is great toward us.”
The verse says that “the truth of the LORD endureth for ever.”
The final command is, “Praise ye the LORD.”

answers: His merciful kindness is great and His truth endures forever
He has made the nations wealthy
He has promised an earthly kingdom
medium.explanation: The verse connects praise with the LORD’s great kindness and enduring truth.
medium.q: Why does the verse give a reason for praising the LORD?

answers: The LORD’s gracious and compassionate goodness
medium.explanation: “Merciful kindness” describes the LORD’s gracious and compassionate goodness.
The phrase means that the LORD’s truth continues forever.

answers: His kindness is abundant, and His truth is everlasting
His kindness is weak, and His truth is temporary
His kindness is hidden, and His truth is uncertain
challenge.explanation: “Great” stresses the abundance of His kindness, while “for ever” stresses the lasting nature of His truth.
challenge.q: What contrast is made between “great” and “for ever”?

answers: His character provides a reason to praise Him
The subject suddenly changes to warfare
The command rejects the preceding statements
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s great kindness and everlasting truth give clear reasons for praise.
challenge.q: Why does “Praise ye the LORD” appropriately follow the description of His kindness and truth?

challenge.explanation: The verse specifically emphasizes that the LORD’s truth endures forever.
challenge.q: Which detail about the LORD’s truth could be easiest to overlook?
